text:
Vancouver was level at 2-2 late in the second period, and the chances said that was about right. Then the Rangers scored 1:29 after Elias Pettersson's shorthanded goal tied it, Tye Kartye finishing a Vladislav Gavrikov assist at 18:25, and the game tilted for good. New York got 1.51 expected goals in the third to Vancouver's 0.24, and the final margin of 6-2 reflects that stretch more than the first 40 minutes, when the Rangers led only 2.13 to 1.39 in chance quality.

Overall, New York produced 3.64 expected goals to Vancouver's 1.62, and simulated replays of every shot give the Rangers the win 82 percent of the time. Shot attempts were nearly even (56 for New York, 54 for Vancouver), so the gap came from shot quality, not volume. The Rangers also won 31 of 50 faceoffs, and Kartye's two goals were worth 0.49 expected goals on his own shots. Will Cuylle scored twice as well, and J.T. Miller picked up two assists with a team-leading 1.75 expected goals share while he was on the ice.

Vancouver's goals came from low-percentage looks: Jake DeBrusk's snap shot had a 4 percent chance, and Pettersson's shorthanded wrister 9 percent. Kevin Lankinen allowed 6 goals on 3.64 expected, 2.36 more than the shots warranted. At the other end, Dylan Garand gave up 2 on 1.62 expected. Alexis Lafrenière scored on the power play at 1:04 of the third, and Gabe Perreault's tip-in at 5:57 made it 5-2, ending any real chance of a comeback.
